author: Joshua Fluke
description:
Corporate bootlicking is getting completely out of control.

Apparently you shouldn't ask for a day off until you're making $300,000 a year because your first priority should be your manager, the company, the CEO and the shareholders — not your own life.

Then we get the perfect example of why that mindset is ridiculous.

One employee gave a multi-million-dollar corporation 14 years of his life, and his farewell party was three boxes of pizza, a construction-paper sign taped to the wall, and a reminder that everyone only gets two slices.

And somehow people in the comments were defending the COMPANY.

In this video, we're talking about corporate loyalty, hustle culture, work-life balance, employee appreciation, company loyalty, toxic workplace expectations and the strange people who think employees should give everything they have to a business while expecting almost nothing in return.

A job is an exchange.

You provide your time, skills and results.
The company provides compensation
title: CORPORATE BOOTLICKING IS OUT OF CONTROL!
